title: Nephi Urges His Brothers to Return
summary: Nephi urges his brothers to return to Jerusalem, be faithful, and be strong like Moses. They remain angry and murmur, but follow him to outside Jerusalem’s walls.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi speaks to his brothers and urges them to go up again to Jerusalem and keep the Lord’s commandments.
Nephi recalls Moses, the divided Red Sea, the fathers’ escape on dry ground, and Pharaoh’s armies drowning.
Nephi says an angel has spoken to his brothers and that the Lord can deliver them and destroy Laban as he did the Egyptians.
His brothers remain angry and murmur, but follow him until they come outside Jerusalem’s walls.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi speaks while his brothers listen.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise place where Nephi speaks and the brothers’ appearance, clothing, and expressions.

spoken_dialogue.text: Let us go up again unto Jerusalem, and let us be faithful in keeping the commandments of the Lord;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: let us be strong like unto Moses;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The account of Moses and the Red Sea is recalled in Nephi’s speech, not shown as a separate present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moses, the Red Sea crossing, an angel, or the destruction of Laban as occurring in this scene.

title: Nephi Enters Jerusalem
summary: At night, Nephi has his brothers hide outside the walls, enters the city, and approaches Laban’s house. Led by the Spirit without knowing beforehand what to do, he finds Laban fallen to the earth, drunken with wine, and draws Laban’s sword.

explicit_facts.text: At night, Nephi has his brothers hide outside the walls, then enters the city and goes toward Laban’s house.
Nephi says he was led by the Spirit without knowing beforehand what he should do.
Near Laban’s house, Nephi sees a man fallen to the earth because he is drunken with wine; Nephi identifies him as Laban.
Nephi draws Laban’s sword and describes its pure-gold hilt and precious-steel blade.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nighttime darkness is visible as Nephi enters the city.
unspecified_visual_details: The Spirit’s appearance, if any; the city’s architecture; the sword’s precise design.

narration.text: I was led by the Spirit, not knowing beforehand the things which I should do.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Spirit’s leading is stated, but no visible form or manifestation is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the Spirit a visible body or appearance.

title: Nephi Hesitates
summary: Nephi feels constrained by the Spirit to kill Laban, but shrinks from doing so. The Spirit speaks to him, citing the Lord’s delivery of Laban into his hands and the Lord’s righteous purposes.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi feels constrained by the Spirit to kill Laban, but says he has never shed human blood and shrinks from slaying him.
The Spirit tells Nephi that the Lord has delivered Laban into his hands and recalls Laban’s attempt to take Nephi’s life, refusal to hearken to the commandments, and taking of their property.
The Spirit again commands Nephi to slay Laban.
The Spirit states that the Lord slays the wicked to bring forth righteous purposes and that one man should perish rather than a nation dwindle and perish in unbelief.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi hesitates beside Laban while holding the sword.
unspecified_visual_details: The Spirit’s appearance and whether its speech is heard aloud or inwardly.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold the Lord hath delivered him into thy hands.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Spirit

spoken_dialogue.text: Slay him, for the Lord hath delivered him into thy hands;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Spirit

spoken_dialogue.text: It is better that one man should perish than that a nation should dwindle and perish in unbelief.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Spirit

narration.text: Never at any time have I shed the blood of man.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Spirit’s speech is a teaching and command, not a visual supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show an embodied Spirit or a separate visible visitation.

title: Nephi Remembers the Plates
summary: Nephi remembers the Lord’s promise concerning his seed and the land of promise. He thinks that his descendants need the law to keep the commandments, that it is engraved on the plates of brass, and that he must obtain the records.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi remembers the Lord’s words that his seed will prosper in the land of promise if they keep the commandments.
Nephi thinks his descendants cannot keep the commandments according to the law of Moses unless they have the law.
Nephi knows the law is engraved on the plates of brass.
Nephi understands that the Lord delivered Laban into his hands so he might obtain the records according to the Lord’s commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi pauses in thought beside Laban.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the plates or remembered words are visually represented.

narration.text: Inasmuch as thy seed shall keep my commandments, they shall prosper in the land of promise.
the law was engraven upon the plates of brass.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi recounts remembered words and private thoughts; neither is a separate present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a vision or portray the plates as present in this moment.

title: Nephi Takes Laban’s Garments
summary: Nephi obeys the voice of the Spirit, takes Laban by the hair, and smites off his head with Laban’s sword. He then puts on Laban’s garments and girds Laban’s armor about his loins.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi takes Laban by the hair and smites off his head with Laban’s sword.
Nephi takes Laban’s garments, puts them on, and girds Laban’s armor about his loins.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The action may be shown without depicting gore, wounds, blood, or severed body parts.
unspecified_visual_details: The garments and armor’s exact design.

narration.text: Therefore I did obey the voice of the Spirit,

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore, blood, wounds, or the severed head.

title: Nephi Meets Laban’s Servant
summary: Wearing Laban’s garments and sword, Nephi goes toward the treasury and meets Laban’s servant, who has the keys. The servant supposes Nephi is Laban. Nephi speaks as if he were Laban, says he will carry the brass plates to his elder brothers outside the walls, and tells the servant to follow. The servant follows, supposing Nephi is Laban and that the brethren are of the church.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi goes toward Laban’s treasury and sees Laban’s servant, who has the treasury keys; Nephi commands him in Laban’s voice to go with him into the treasury.
The servant supposes Nephi is his master Laban because of the garments and sword.
The servant speaks to Nephi about the elders of the Jews, knowing Laban had been among them by night.
Nephi speaks to the servant as if he were Laban, says he will carry the brass-plate engravings to his elder brothers outside the walls, and bids the servant follow.
The servant supposes Nephi is the Laban he had slain and follows him; on the way to Nephi’s brothers, the servant speaks many times about the elders of the Jews.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The servant carries or holds the keys, without requiring a particular design.
unspecified_visual_details: The treasury’s appearance; the servant’s appearance and clothing; the plates’ appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: that I should carry the engravings, which were upon the plates of brass, to my elder brethren, who were without the walls.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The servant’s mistaken belief is reported; do not portray it as a separate scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add dialogue for the servant; his words are summarized, not quoted.

title: The Brothers Flee, Then Stop
summary: Laman, Lemuel, and Sam see Nephi and are frightened, supposing he is Laban who has slain Nephi and seeks their lives. They flee, then stop when they hear Nephi call after them. Laban’s servant trembles and is about to flee back to Jerusalem; Nephi seizes and holds him.

explicit_facts.text: Laman, Lemuel, and Sam are frightened when they see Nephi and flee, supposing he is Laban who has slain Nephi and seeks their lives.
Nephi calls after them; they hear him and cease fleeing.
Laban’s servant trembles and is about to flee back to Jerusalem.
Nephi, a man large in stature and strengthened by the Lord, seizes and holds the servant so he cannot flee.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The brothers can be shown stopping as they recognize Nephi’s call.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise position of each person and their appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: And it came to pass that I called after them,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the brothers’ mistaken belief as a separate event.

title: Zoram Promises to Go
summary: Nephi promises to spare the servant’s life if he hearkens, tells him not to fear, and offers him freedom and a place with them if he goes to Nephi’s father in the wilderness. The servant is named Zoram; he agrees and swears to stay with them. Nephi’s party wants this so the Jews will not learn of their flight and pursue them. Their fears concerning Zoram cease after his oath.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi promises the servant that they will spare his life if he hearkens to their words.
Nephi swears that the servant need not fear and will be a free man like them if he goes with them into the wilderness.
Nephi says the Lord has commanded them and offers the servant a place with them if he goes to Nephi’s father in the wilderness.
The servant is named Zoram; he takes courage, promises to go to Nephi’s father, and makes an oath to remain with them.
They want Zoram to remain with them so the Jews will not learn of their flight and pursue and destroy them.
After Zoram makes an oath, their fears concerning him cease.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and Zoram face one another as Nephi makes his offer and Zoram responds.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact setting of the exchange and any gestures accompanying the oath.

spoken_dialogue.text: that if he would hearken unto my words, as the Lord liveth, and as I live, even so that if he would hearken unto our words, we would spare his life.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: Surely the Lord hath commanded us to do this thing;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The reason for keeping Zoram with them is narrated as their concern, not spoken dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent Zoram’s exact oath wording.

title: They Depart with the Plates
summary: They take the brass plates and Zoram, depart into the wilderness, and journey to their father’s tent.

explicit_facts.text: They take the brass plates and Laban’s servant, depart into the wilderness, and journey to their father’s tent.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The party travels together carrying the plates.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, travel conditions, and appearance of the plates.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show their arrival at the tent as a separate later event beyond the stated journey.
